accepted_recoveries: Raise the search CPU request and limit to the benchmark's known-safe values after capacity checks.
Raise CPU capacity and tune the liveness timeout or failure threshold to the known-good fixture without disabling health detection.
forbidden_actions: Do not remove the liveness probe.
Do not set an unlimited CPU policy.
Do not lower benchmark traffic or weaken SLO measurement.
incident.injected_fault: The search container is capped at 100m CPU while its liveness probe has a one-second timeout, causing sustained throttling, probe timeouts, and restart cascades under load.
observable_signals: Container CPU throttling rises sharply during benchmark traffic.
Liveness probes time out and kubelet restarts otherwise functional search containers.
HTTP p95 latency and 5xx rate worsen in step with throttling and restarts.
preconditions: The load generator applies the same fixed profile before and after recovery.
Nodes and namespace quota have room for the known-safe CPU settings.
The search application has no independent dependency failure.
required_evidence: Capture CPU usage, CFS throttled periods, request, and limit.
Capture liveness probe settings and kubelet Unhealthy events.
Correlate throttling, probe failures, restarts, and request latency on one timeline.
Verify rollout stability and all SLO windows under the same load.

hypotheses.cause: The search container CPU limit and request are capped at 100m, causing severe CFS CPU throttling under load. When /healthz executes its 50ms CPU burn, probe execution exceeds the 1-second timeout, leading to liveness probe failures and container restart cascades.
supports: Pod container resources specify cpu requests and limits at 100m with annotation proofix.io/profile: injected-100m-cpu.
SearchServer.java health endpoint burns 50,000 microseconds (50ms) of CPU time, exceeding the 1s liveness timeout under concurrent load and 100m CPU capping.

Kubelet events show repeated 'Liveness probe failed: Get http://10.42.0.131:8080/healthz: context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)' and 'Container search-api failed liveness probe, will be restarted'.
Pod status records container restartCount of 4 with last termination exitCode 143 (SIGTERM from kubelet).

hypotheses.cause: Application-level deadlock or JVM heap memory exhaustion causing the HTTP server to hang and fail liveness probe responses.
contradicts: SearchServer.java contains lock-free request handlers without synchronized blocks or deadlocking concurrency primitives.
JVM heap is configured with -Xms32m -Xmx128m within a 256Mi container limit, and termination reason is not OOMKilled (exitCode 143).
Startup probe initially passed before load generation began.
supports: Liveness probe failed due to context deadline exceeded awaiting HTTP headers on port 8080.

hypotheses.cause: Flannel CNI or kubelet networking failure preventing probe traffic from reaching pod IP 10.42.0.131.
contradicts: Single node vm-4 is Ready with no network or resource pressure conditions.
Connection refused errors occurred only transiently while the container was being killed (exitCode 143) and restarting.
Kubelet and pod run on the same node vm-4 without overlay routing failure.
supports: Events report transient 'dial tcp 10.42.0.131:8080: connect: connection refused' probe errors.

payload.rationale: The search-api container is constrained to 100m CPU requests and limits, causing severe CFS quota throttling under load. The /healthz endpoint executes a 50ms CPU burn which, under concurrent search traffic, fails to finish within the 1-second liveness probe timeout. This triggers consecutive liveness probe failures, killing the container (SIGTERM/exit code 143) and causing a restart cascade. Increasing the CPU request to 500m and CPU limit to 1000m provides sufficient capacity for health check execution alongside search requests, preventing probe timeouts and container restarts.
payload.rollback_trigger: If pod rollout fails, resource quota/node allocation errors occur, or restart cascades persist with HTTP 5xx rate >= 0.001 or p95 latency >= 200ms.

success_criteria.description: Deployment search-api successfully rolls out a healthy pod, liveness probe timeouts and container restarts cease, and the service meets SLO requirements with p95 latency < 200ms and HTTP 5xx error rate < 0.001 across consecutive evaluation windows.

data.error: RuntimeError: kubectl command failed (1): The Deployment "search-api" is invalid: spec.template.spec.containers[0].image: Required value

payload.rationale: The previous patch failed with 'spec.template.spec.containers[0].image: Required value' because it used JSON merge patch semantics ('merge'), which replaces the entire containers array and drops required fields like image. Changing the patch_type to 'strategic' enables strategic merge patch semantics, correctly merging the resource requests (500m) and limits (1000m) into the existing search-api container specification without wiping out other container fields. This resolves the CPU throttling causing liveness probe timeouts.
payload.rollback_trigger: HTTP 5xx rate exceeds 0.001, p95 latency exceeds 200ms, or search-api deployment rollout fails.

success_criteria.description: The search-api deployment rolls out successfully, liveness probes pass consistently without timeouts, container restart count stops increasing, HTTP 5xx rate remains below 0.001, and p95 latency remains below 200ms for at least 3 consecutive windows.
